AMENDMENT TO ORDINANCE 93-03, ARTICLE VIII, SECTION(S) 8-1(F)(3); 8-2(F)(3); 8-4(F)(4).

AN ORDINANCE TO PROVIDE SETBACKS FOR CERTAIN ACCESSORY BUILDINGS, TO PROVIDE FOR CERTAIN EXCEPTIONS; TO PROVIDE FOR A MAXIMUM HEIGHT FOR ACCESSORY BUILDINGS; TO PROVIDE FOR REVIEW BY THE TOWN MANAGER; TO AMEND ARTICLE VIII, SECTION(S) 8-1(F)(3); 8-2(F)G); 8-4(F)(4); AND FOR OTHER LAWFUL PURPOSES.
3: - 3. Setbacks: Front - sixty-five feet from the center line of the street or road in front or forty feet from the property line, whichever is greater; Rear - twenty-five feet from the rear property line; Side - fifteen feet from each side line. Corner Lots - minimum setback adjacent to the side of the residence shall be thirty feet from the property line or fifty-five feet from the center line of the side street, whichever is greater. Accessory buildings which contain 300 square feet or less of floor space shall be a minimum of 2 feet from the back and side property lines. The building shall be a minimum of 65 feet from the center line of the highway on the front side of the property. Except that any well-house or like building may be placed within 65 feet of the center line of the highway. No accessory building shall exceed 12 feet in height at its peak. The placement of any accessory building as immediately described above is subject to review by the Town Manager. The Town Manager shall review the placement for purposes of determining whether or not the building interferes with the flow of traffic by blocking views of the road.
6: - 3. Setbacks: Single Family - Front: sixty-five feet from the centerline of the street or road in front or forty feet from the property line, whichever is greater; Rear: twenty-five feet from the rear property line; Side: fifteen feet from each side property line; Corner Lots: minimum setback adjacent to the side of the residence shall be thirty feet from the property line or fifty-five feet from the center line of the side street, whichever is greater. Accessory buildings which contain 300 square feet or less of floor space shall be a minimum of 2 feet from the back and side property lines. The building shall be a minimum of 65 feet from the center line of the highway on the front side of the property. Except that any well-house or like building may be placed within 65 feet of the center line of the highway. No accessory building shall exceed 12 feet in height at its peak. The placement of any accessory building as immediately described above is subject to review by the Town Manager. The Town Manager shall review the placement for purposes of determining whether or not the building interferes with the flow of traffic by blocking views of the road. Duplex - Same as for single family. Triplex - Same as for single family. Multi-family - Front: 75 feet from centerline of street, road or highway in front or 55 feet from property line whichever is greater; Sides: 40 feet from property line and 30 feet from any other building; Rear: 40 feet from property line. Accessory Buildings: only one accessory building per dwelling unit is permitted, such accessory building not to exceed 144 square feet of floor space.

- 4. Accessory Buildings: only one customary accessory building shall be allowed on each lot. Setbacks for accessory buildings: Accessory buildings which contain 300 square feet or less of floor space shall be a minimum of 2 feet from the back and side property lines. The building shall be a minimum of 65 feet from the center line of the highway on the front side of the property. Except that any well- house or like building may be placed within 65 feet of the center line of the

highway. No accessory building shall exceed 12 feet in height at its peak. The placement of any accessory building as immediately described above is subject to review by the Town Manager. The Town Manager shall review the placement for purposes of determining whether or not the building interferes with the flow of traffic by blocking views of the road.
8:
This Ordinance is created by the Mayor and Town Council pursuant to the authority granted under the Town Charter, Home Rule Powers, and the Constitution of the State of

Georgia.
9: Should any section or provision of this Ordinance be declared by the courts to be unconstitutional or invalid, such decision shall not affect the validity of the ordinance, as a whole or any part thereof, other than the parts that are declared to be unconstitutional or invalid.
10: Where there is an apparent conflict in this Ordinance between specific and general provisions, it is the intention hereof that the specific provision shall control.
11: All Ordinances and parts of Ordinances in conflict herewith are hereby repealed.
12:
The effective date of this Ordinance shall be upon approval of the Mayor and Town

Council of the Town of Clermont, Georgia.
